title: Differentials of a smooth morphism are free near a point, of rank the fibre dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$ with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the fibre of $f$ over $s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $x'\in X_s$ the point of $X_s$ lying over $x$. Then $d:=\dim_{x'}(X_s)$ [def-kun-dimension] is a non-negative integer, and there are affine open subschemes $V\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $x\in W$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$ such that, with $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $R\to A$ the ring map corresponding to $f|_W:W\to V$, the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a free $A$-module of rank $d$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02G1 (label lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free, line 7214: for f smooth, Omega_{X/S} is finite locally free with rank_x(Omega_{X/S}) = dim_x(X_{f(x)})), read on an affine open W = Spec A over V = Spec R where Omega_{X/S}|_W is the sheaf of Omega_{A/R} (Lemma 01UT, label lemma-differentials-affine, line 6441) and shrunk to a principal open on which this finite locally free module is free; smoothness in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is that of Morphisms Definition 01V5 by more-morphisms.tex Lemma 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth)

proof.text: (Affine opens on which $f$ is standard smooth.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-locally-standard-smooth] applied to the smooth morphism $f$ and the point $x$ there are affine open subschemes $V\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $x\in W$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$ such that, with $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $\varphi:R\to A$ the ring map induced by $f$ (the ring map corresponding to $f|_W:W\to V$), the $R$-algebra $A$ has a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]: integers $n\ge c\ge0$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ under which $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{1\le i,j\le c}$ maps to a unit of $A$. These $V$, $W$ are the affine opens of the statement; it remains to show $\dim_{x'}(X_s)=n-c$ and that $\Omega_{A/R}$ is free of rank $n-c$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free, line 7214): 'The statement is local on X and S. By Lemma 01V7 (lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth) above we may assume that f is a standard smooth morphism of affines'

proof.text: (The differentials are free of rank $n-c$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis] applied to the standard smooth presentation of step 1, the $A$-module $\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free with basis $\mathrm da_{c+1},\dots,\mathrm da_n$, $a_i\in A$ the image of $x_i$; so $\Omega_{A/R}\cong A^{n-c}$ is a free $A$-module of rank $n-c$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), part (2), as invoked in the proof of Morphisms Lemma 02G1 ('In this case the result follows from Algebra, Lemma 00T7')

proof.text: (The fibre near $x'$ is the spectrum of the fibre ring.) Let $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ and $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ be the canonical open immersions with images $W$ and $V$, and $\mathfrak q\subset A$, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ primes with $\iota_W(\mathfrak q)=x$, $\iota_V(\mathfrak p)=s$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=f\circ\iota_W$; as $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ sends $\mathfrak q$ to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\iota_V$ is injective, $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Let $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and $t=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\pi:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to S$. Since $\iota_V$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] it induces an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{S,s}\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak p}$ and hence of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]; composed with the isomorphism $e$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] (which identifies $\operatorname{Spec}\pi$ with the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$) this gives an isomorphism $\theta:\kappa(s)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $t=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}\theta$, $j_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ the canonical morphism [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. As $\operatorname{Spec}\theta$ is an isomorphism over $S$, the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is isomorphic, compatibly with the first projections to $X$, to $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ formed with $t$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; write $p_1:X_s\to X$ for the first projection, so $p_1(x')=x$. Since $t$ factors through $V$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (opens $W\subseteq X$, $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ itself, $V\subseteq S$) shows that $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to X_s$ is an open immersion with image the open $O=p_1^{-1}(W)\ni x'$, compatible with the projections to $X$. Via the isomorphisms $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}A\cong W$, $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}R\cong V$ (compatible with $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ by the square above), $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the first projection becoming $\operatorname{Spec}j$, $j:A\to C$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. So there is a homeomorphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}C\to O$ with $p_1\circ h=\iota_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}j$. Let $\mathfrak Q=h^{-1}(x')$; then $\iota_W(j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q))=p_1(x')=x=\iota_W(\mathfrak q)$, so $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$. Finally $\dim_{x'}(X_s)=\dim_{x'}(O)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] ($O$ open in $X_s$), and a homeomorphism carries open neighbourhoods to open neighbourhoods and strict chains of irreducible closed subsets to strict chains of the same length, so $\dim_{x'}(O)=\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}C)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point, def-kun-dimension]. Hence $\dim_{x'}(X_s)=\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}C)$.

source.place: The locality 'The statement is local on X and S' of the proof of Morphisms Lemma 02G1, written out: Schemes, Lemma 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product, line 3198: open subschemes of a fibre product), Lemma 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines: fibre product of affines is Spec of the tensor product), Lemma 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological, line 3511: points of the fibre); Topology, Definition 0055 (definition-Krull) and the remark after it (dimension at a point computed on small open neighbourhoods)

proof.text: (The fibre ring has dimension $n-c$ at every point; conclusion.) The ring isomorphism $C=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes a$, gives a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA)\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; let $\mathfrak Q'$ correspond to $\mathfrak Q$, so $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}C)=\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}(\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA))$ as in step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-base-change] applied to the standard smooth presentation of step 1 and $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA$ has a standard smooth presentation $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1^\pi,\dots,f_c^\pi)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA$ with the same $n\ge c\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. Since $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a field, [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-over-field-dimension-at-points] gives $\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}(\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA))=n-c$. With step 3, $d=\dim_{x'}(X_s)=n-c$, a non-negative integer because $n\ge c$. By step 2, $\Omega_{A/R}$ is a free $A$-module of rank $n-c=d$, for the affine opens $V$, $W$ of step 1, which contain $s$ and $x$ and satisfy $f(W)\subseteq V$. This is the statement.
